problem_text:
A transportation provider plans a set of profitable operations by selecting a consistent set of discrete choices. Each choice represents committing to an option, a linkage, or an activity segment, and every choice has a net cost that can be positive (expense) or negative (profit credit).

A central feature of this instance is consistency across multiple representations of the same underlying commitment. There are 23296 synchronization links; each link forces two choices to take the same on/off status, ensuring that mirrored representations stay aligned.

In addition, there are 588 balance groups that enforce that two equally-sized pools of choices stay in equilibrium: within each group, the number of selected choices on the “positive side” must match the number selected on the “negative side”.

The plan must avoid incompatible combinations captured by 12138 conflict groups (at most one choice may be selected in each group). It must also satisfy minimum selection expectations across 52 coverage groups (at least a required number of members must be selected).

Further, there are 1260 cap rules that limit how many items may be selected within certain protected subsets.

Finally, the instance contains 4 policy dimensions that limit how concentrated a certain attribute may be among selected choices, and a small set of additional linear rules that do not fit the higher-level families.

The goal is to select a consistent set of choices that respects all operational rules and yields the minimum total net cost.
